report:
### Conclusion
There is no scientific evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19. Global health organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO), and medical researchers have repeatedly debunked this claim.

### Evidence & Analysis

* **Theoretical Basis:** Garlic contains bioactive organosulfur compounds, such as allicin, which exhibit general antibacterial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties in laboratory settings (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9953069/). These general health properties led to widespread viral rumors during the pandemic.
* **Lack of Clinical Evidence:** Laboratory properties do not equate to a clinical cure for human viral infections. No human clinical trials demonstrate that garlic water effectively treats or cures SARS-CoV-2 infection (https://factcheck.afp.com/theres-no-scientific-proof-tonic-onions-ginger-garlic-and-lemon-can-cure-covid-19).
* **Impact of Heat:** Allicin is heat-sensitive and degrades rapidly when exposed to high temperatures. Boiling garlic actually breaks down its active compounds, reducing any potential bioactivity (https://www.naturallywith.com/5-myths-influence-of-garlic-and-covid-19/).
* **Expert Consensus:** Fact-checking organizations and public health authorities emphasize that while garlic can be part of a healthy diet, home remedies like boiled garlic water cannot prevent, treat, or cure COVID-19 (https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/fact-check/264621-heat-garlic-ginger-cure-covid-19/).

### Sources
* AFP Fact Check: https://factcheck.afp.com/theres-no-scientific-proof-tonic-onions-ginger-garlic-and-lemon-can-cure-covid-19
* PMC / Molecular Screening Study: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9953069/
* NaturallyWith / Garlic & COVID-19: https://www.naturallywith.com/5-myths-influence-of-garlic-and-covid-19/
